title: The boss fight's next round landed on refactor-run: the gunship's three guns, SOL's tracking wall, the fright and the stun, the arena with its push-out; the health is 180 from a dodging survival run (31.0 s), a held creature dies in 27.8 s, and the walls cost 0.53 to 0.59 ms a frame
context: The design is 2026-10-08-boss-fight-next-round-design (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-boss-fight-next-round-design.md). The prototype's health 155 killed a held creature in 24.22 s with the four guns; the new fight has a creature that flees and a tank that keeps out of the rings, so the balance was set from a survival run in the lab: the acceptance handle's dodge (circle at 45 m, widened while a nuke's ring shows, back after it lands) with every shooter, the fear and the arena on, until KILLED. The walls were measured as the spec requires (section 3).
outcome: Built in ten commits on refactor-run, never pushed: 972afeed (the body rules to src/labs/boss/body.js), cd4a1843 (the rules fire the three guns), 881c4438 (the fright and the stun), 8ca81652 (the arena's geometry), f8e98d83, 3a7f2eac (the lab fires the guns and SOL), 858b4a7b, 0b00f6e9 (the lab frightens), d659cee3 (the arena in the lab) and bae8296f (the measurement and the balance), plus the records. BALANCE: the survival run killed the creature at 26.26 s and 26.03 s of fight clock at health 155 (mean 26.15, taken 0), so health = round5(155 x 30 / 26.15) = 180; confirmed at 180 in two full --boss-fight runs: KILLED at 31.03 s and 31.03 s (3 frights, 3 stuns, taken 0). The held-still anchor in node (test/boss-fight.mjs, instinct off, the 44 floor contacts, the tank far): 27.80 s at 180 (24.22 s at 155); the bound is 27.8 s +- 20 %; the browser's standing body died at 27.83 and 27.98 s. WALLS (--boss-walls: no shooters, the creature's target pinned on w1's middle with the routing off, 10 s of lab clock, three runs): the push-out costs 0.135, 0.132 and 0.147 ms a solver step, 0.540, 0.527 and 0.587 ms a frame (four steps a frame; the spec's acceptance is under 1 ms); 15.9, 15.8 and 15.7 nodes are pushed on the last step of a frame over the last 3 s (10.0 over the whole 10 s, at most 30); the jitter, the mean frame-to-frame displacement of a pushed node over the last 3 s, is 0.074, 0.112 and 0.115 m (the largest single move 3.0 to 8.0 m, a node that changes side of the wall between frames); taken 0 in every run. In a full fight the arena's mean step cost is 0.12 to 0.17 ms and up to 52 to 60 nodes are pushed. THE WALL BY EYE (one chase-view screenshot of w1 at six seconds of the run): the wall stands upright and flat on the ground, face-on to the camera as expected for a 30 degree yaw seen from the tank behind it (the line of sight is within two degrees of perpendicular to the wall's length), the body stands behind it with two legs reaching to its ends and no limb or body visible through the wall; the far-side feet cannot be seen from the chase camera. THE PLAYER WHO DODGES: two earlier dodge versions were LOST and are not measurements: the first never widened (it read the fight clock; the plans carry the lab's clock), the second widened to a flat 75 m and was still taken by the first MK-9 at 24.2 s, because the MK-9's point lies 15 m behind the centre plus the creature's velocity lead (up to about 25 m off the centre at its landing) so a 75 m circle about the centre passes within 55 m of it; the handle's dodge now widens to max(75 m, the point's distance from the centre + 55 m + the hull + 3 m), about 85 to 90 m, and returns to 45 m after the landing. FOR THE OWNER'S PLAYTEST: (1) the nuke's 55 m ring against the tank: staying outside it asks for a tank 85 m or more out on a ring whose point drifts with the creature's lead, and the tank is lost to the first MK-9 at 24 s if it is not dodged; is that fair, or should the ring or the lead shrink; (2) the fright's feel: how often it runs (3 to 5 frights and 3 to 4 stuns in a 26 to 31 s fight) and whether the flight reads as fear or as dithering; (3) the push-out's look: nodes are moved to the wall's surface after each step, so a body pressed against a wall should look pressed, not torn; (4) a known cosmetic residual: when the tank parks 6 to 14 m behind a wall the creature's routed waypoint sits on the wall's 16 m circle and it dithers about 2 m there. THIN SPOTS: the circling step's half-by-24 s check passes on the rate (3.99 hp/s against 3.75 needed at health 180; at 155 the hp fell below half at 18.6 s); a circling run (not dodging) was lost to a Bofors round at 15 s once (browser physics is not deterministic; it passed on the rerun). Gates: npm test (217 programs), npm run check, npm run build and npm run log:check green; --boss-fight and --boss-walls green from a frozen snapshot.
alternatives: A flat 75 m widening for the dodge, as first specified: the survival run was LOST to the first MK-9 at 24.2 s, so it measured nothing.
Health 155 kept: the dodging survival kill at 26.15 s is below the owner's thirty seconds.
